entry.title: 26.10.200¶ (TriplyDB–Changelog)
entry.content:
Release date: 2026-10-28

Our documentation has been rewritten. It is organised by what you come to do: tutorials, how-to guides, reference and concepts. Start with Get started with TriplyDB or TriplyDB at a glance.

From this release on, this changelog also lists the changes to features in preview, each entry marked like thisPreview. A preview feature is switched on per instance, by arrangement: get in touch if you would like access. Three features are in preview:

  • Flows: data pipelines that live inside TriplyDB, drawn on a canvas from tasks such as an import, a query or a SHACL validation, and run by hand, on a schedule or when data is uploaded. See Flows and Build your first flow.
  • MCP server: connects an AI assistant to TriplyDB, so it can answer questions about your datasets and work with them for you. See Connect an AI assistant and the MCP server reference.
  • The redesigned console: a new interface for TriplyDB.

Features

  • ConsoleEmails sent by TriplyDB, such as the notice of a new API token, follow the look of the console.
  • PreviewMCPBreakingAn AI assistant identifies itself with a Client ID Metadata Document: an HTTPS URL where it publishes its own details, and whose host the consent screen shows. Dynamic Client Registration is no longer supported, so clients using the deprecated spec can no longer connect. Every connected assistant asks you to authorize it once more after the upgrade. #13642
  • PreviewMCPAI assistants can work with flows: read, create and update a flow, read its earlier versions, run it, follow its runs, and manage its schedules. #13649
  • PreviewMCPThe MCP server speaks revision 2026-07-28 of the MCP specification. Clients that speak revision 2025-11-25 keep working. #13241
  • PreviewFlowsA SHACL Validate task sets a conforms variable, so a decision after it can branch on whether the data conforms. #13087
  • PreviewData EditorThe DCAT view lists datasets, data services, distributions and other catalog resources that no catalog leads to in a section of their own, "Not reachable from a catalog", grouped by class. #14953
  • PreviewConsoleThe redesigned console works better on narrow screens, loads the content page faster by fetching filter counts only while the Filters tab is open, and has a polished Data Editor and Data Model. #12721 · #14885 · #14991

Issues fixed

  • SPARQLA query without triple patterns, such as one built only from values and bind, ignored being stopped and its own timeout, affecting the response time of other queries. #14977
  • SPARQLTSV results wrote an xsd:decimal without a decimal point, such as 1, as a bare number, which a TSV reader takes for an xsd:integer. The doubles INF and NaN were written bare as well, which is no valid number. Such values are now written in full, with their datatype. #14993
  • ServicesA Virtuoso query that ran out of its time limit occasionally answered with a server error instead of 400 Bad Request.
  • Data EditorA value with leading or trailing whitespace could not be removed. The edit was recorded in the history, but the value stayed. #14887
  • PreviewFlowsA run that failed reported only "Something went wrong". It shows the error that stopped it. #13371
  • PreviewFlowsA run that failed while starting, or that timed out, sent no failure email. The failure email is also easier to read. #11471 · #14767
  • PreviewFlowsA SPARQL Update task could fail for large queries. #14686
  • PreviewFlowsThe saved-query selector of a SPARQL Update task hid update queries that use an API variable, although they ran. #11493
  • PreviewFlowsThe suggestions in the flow builder did not reflect a change to a dataset, query or other resource a flow uses until the page was reloaded. #12909

entry.title: 26.10.100¶ (TriplyDB–Changelog)
entry.content:
Release date: 2026-10-14

Features

  • Access ControlGroups can now carry an access level. The access level of the contents within that group (datasets, queries, stories) may not exceed the access level of the group itself. #14832
  • Access ControlTwo new admin settings bound the access levels on the instance: a maximum access level, which lowers every more open group and resource to it, and a default access level for new groups and resources. The default is private. #14832
  • Access ControlBreakingA group created without an explicit access level now starts out private rather than public. A script (TriplyDB.js, TriplyETL, the API) that creates a group and then a public dataset, query or story in it fails with 403 Forbidden, because a resource cannot be more open than its group. Pass accessLevel: "public" when creating the group, or have an administrator raise the default access level. Existing groups keep their access level. #14832
  • Access ControlAnonymous visitors only see a user account when that user publishes something: a public dataset, saved query, story or SPARQL proxy. This applies to account pages, account listings and group member lists. #14832
  • GroupsDeleting a group, deleting a user, or making a group's access level stricter no longer requires clearing everything that stands in the way first. After one confirmation, a stricter access level is applied to everything in the group and its subgroups, deleting a group deletes its subgroups and their contents, and deleting a user deletes the groups they solely own (unless owners of a parent group can take them over). The confirmation counts what will be affected, and nothing changes if you lack permission on any of it. #14937
  • ServicesVirtuoso services now run Virtuoso 7.2.17. This release comes with the latest patches and security fixes. There are two noticeable changes: #14165
    • a construct query that exceeds the result limit (10,000 statements by default) fails with an error instead of returning a silently truncated result
    • computed geometries such as those from bif:st_point no longer carry the geo:wktLiteral datatype.

Issues fixed

  • SPARQLNumbers of different datatypes were compared by datatype rather than by value, so "3"^^xsd:decimal = 3 was false. Integers that differ only beyond double precision could not be ordered either. #14846
  • SPARQLA property path from a variable back to itself, such as ?x :p+ ?x, only matched self-loops and missed longer cycles. #14952
  • Data ModelProperty shapes with the same sh:path showed up as separate properties, and the Data Editor ignored part of their configuration. This affected application profiles that extend a standard, such as DCAT-AP-NL or SKOS-AP-NL. #11481
  • Data EditorConstraints checked with SPARQL were evaluated against the stored data only. #14629
  • GroupsA group could lose its last enabled owner, or an instance its last enabled administrator, by disabling, demoting or deleting a user.
  • Access ControlAn owner of a parent group who has a weaker role of their own in a subgroup was shown that subgroup's settings as read-only, although they were allowed to manage it. #13965
  • Access ControlSigning in with Google or GitHub failed on instances whose outbound traffic must go through an HTTP proxy. #14843
  • SPARQLAfter a query timed out, the next query could fail as well.

Patch releases

  • 26.10.104 · 2026-10-21
    • SPARQLA SPARQL update that was cancelled or timed out could leave its query worker occupied for good. Once every worker was occupied, the API answered every query with 503 Service Unavailable until it was restarted. #14970
  • 26.10.103 · 2026-10-21
    • Data UploadBreakingThe root of an uploaded XML, JSON, CSV or TSV file is typed <http://sparql.xyz/facade-x/ns/Root>, where it was typed <http://sparql.xyz/facade-x/ns/root>. Queries that select roots by their class need the new IRI. #14967
    • Data UploadThe text of an XML element containing a CDATA section was split into one literal per piece. It is now a single literal, as the Facade-X XML mapping prescribes. #14967
    • Data UploadA / was appended to an XML namespace name ending in #, so xmlns="http://example.org/ns#" produced IRIs such as http://example.org/ns#/x. #14967
  • 26.10.102 · 2026-10-15
    • Data UploadA large import that produced many graphs failed after indexing had finished. #14958

entry.title: 26.9.200¶ (TriplyDB–Changelog)
entry.content:
Release date: 2026-09-16

Features

  • APITriplyDB implements the SPARQL 1.1 Graph Store HTTP Protocol, at /datasets/{account}/{dataset}/graph-store. A graph can be read with GET (with content negotiation, and conditional requests through ETag and Last-Modified), replaced with PUT, merged into with POST, and removed with DELETE. The writing methods are a bulk-upload route: they impose no size limit and parse the payload as it arrives, so a file that turns out to be malformed on its third line is refused without ever being stored. See the Graphs endpoints in the OpenAPI reference. #9439

Issues fixed

  • Data UploadAn upload that merged into an existing graph and ran for more than two days could lose data. #14225
  • SPARQLA query opening with a property path whose far end a values clause binds, feeding a pattern with a variable predicate, could become several times slower, often leading to timeouts. These now resolve in time. #14345
  • Data UploadUploading XML registered a TriplyDB-specific namespace under the standard xml prefix, so the standard XML namespace could not be configured for a dataset holding uploaded XML. That vendor namespace moved to the txml prefix, xmlns declarations no longer produce triples of their own, and an attribute without a prefix now takes the namespace of the element it belongs to rather than a generic one. #13367
  • SPARQLThe performance of a query could differ under the same conditions it was executed it. This performance difference is now gone, and performance is fully deterministic. #14191
  • SPARQLA query that Virtuoso rejects because of the query itself now answers 400 with Virtuoso's own reason, instead of a generic server error.
  • Saved QueriesRequesting a saved query's metadata or its OpenAPI description without naming a version answered 404 instead of describing the latest version, and asking for either on a query with no saved version at all answered with a document that could not be used.
  • Saved QueriesA SPARQL update sent to a saved query that runs against a dedicated service now explains that updates only run against the dataset itself, instead of failing with a service error.
  • Access ControlDeleting a user who was the only owner of a group failed without saying why. The message now names the group, and is rendered properly in the account settings.

entry.title: 26.9.100¶ (TriplyDB–Changelog)
entry.content:
Release date: 2026-09-02

Features

  • Data UploadJSON files can now be uploaded, and are converted to RDF following the same Facade-X mapping that XML and tabular uploads already use. JSON Lines is supported as well, through the .jsonl and .ndjson extensions. Note that .json files are now read as plain JSON rather than as JSON-LD: use the .jsonld extension for JSON-LD documents. See Supported file formats. #10520
  • SPARQLOptimized query planning, so that sorting (via order by) a smaller intermediate result is cheaper, so queries that sort before an operation which multiplies rows — several triple patterns on the same subject, a union, a property path — get faster. #9715
  • SaaSSSL (https) connections to TriplyDB deployments now negotiate post-quantum key exchange, and the accepted cipher suites have been narrowed to the current recommendations. This guards traffic captured today against decryption by a future quantum computer. #11338

Issues fixed

  • SPARQL-IDEAutocomplete suggestions are slow, causing a decrease in user experience

entry.title: 26.8.200¶ (TriplyDB–Changelog)
entry.content:
Release date: 2026-08-19

Features

  • SPARQLThe query planner now carries known variable bindings across SERVICE and ORDER BY, instead of treating them as a barrier. Joins that follow such an operation can use the bindings established before it, which makes federated queries in particular considerably faster — one benchmark query dropped from 1.4 seconds to 0.49 seconds.

Issues fixed

  • Access ControlAPI tokens could not delete a group any more, and the call failed with 401 Unauthorized. #13613
  • APIThe API response for pinned account items had an unintended breaking schema change, causing possible breakage in third party application #13614
  • SPARQLVery large SPARQL Update queries could fail with a "response too large" error. #13306 · #13500
  • SPARQLAn aggregate ignored a value that its output variable was already bound to, returning every group instead of only the groups that matched. #13449
  • Saved QueriesNavigating away from a saved query with unsaved changes showed the "are you sure" prompt twice. #13429
  • ConsoleLinks that open a dialog — configuring pinned items, adding a user, showing code snippets — replaced the current browser history entry instead of adding one, so the browser's back button could not be used to close the dialog.

entry.title: 26.8.100¶ (TriplyDB–Changelog)
entry.content:
Release date: 2026-08-05

Features

  • SPARQLThe query optimizer now interleaves operations across independent parts of a join, instead of running each part to completion before starting the next. This produces cheaper query plans in some cases; queries are never slower and are sometimes faster. #11638
  • Data UploadEach URL in a "download from URL" job can now carry its own HTTP headers, so data can be imported from sources that require for example an Authorization header. Requests that point at the TriplyDB instance itself automatically reuse the caller's own authorization, and need no header of their own.

Issues fixed

  • InsightsViewing the class-frequency diagram for a graph with no classes (or more classes than the supported limit) could throw an error instead of showing an empty chart. #13056
  • Data ModelThe schema view could show a redundant rdfs:subClassOf edge alongside the owl:equivalentClass edge between the same two classes. #11548
  • APIRequests in progress during a scheduled deploy or maintenance window could occasionally fail with a transient server error. #11433
  • Query JobsA completed select query job's downloaded results reported one more result row than it actually contained, because the JSONL header line was counted as a row.
  • SPARQLThe query planner underestimated the cost of property paths and of aggregates, because it treated variables that only become bound by the operation itself as already bound. This could result in a suboptimal join order. #12858 · #12859

entry.title: 26.6.100¶ (TriplyDB–Changelog)
entry.content:
Release date: 2026-06-11

Features

  • Data ModelClasses that come from an imported ontology but do not yet have a SHACL shape are now shown in the data model and can be edited directly — editing such a class adds a node shape for it in the background. The "create a class" dialog now also blocks accidentally overwriting an existing class. #11440
  • Data EditorAdded support for owl:deprecated. Deprecated classes, properties, and SKOS concepts are now visually marked in the data model and SKOS navigators, so deprecated terms are easy to recognise while editing. #11451

Issues fixed

  • Data EditorThe editor could take several minutes to load on large datasets and emitted 5xx errors while doing so. #11571
  • Query JobsA construct query job could report a green ("finished") status even when importing its results failed (for example when HDT creation ran out of memory), leaving the user with an empty graph and no error. #11602
  • Data UploadIncremental uploads to a large existing graph were slow when merging graphs. #11387
  • Data EditorThe SKOS tree crashed on concept schemes with cyclic hierarchies and showed blank rows for concepts without a label. #11665
  • Data EditorA resource without an rdf:type was incorrectly shown as "Resource not found". #11667
  • Data EditorAutocomplete lookups were cancelled when the browser window lost focus, so suggestions failed to appear after switching back to the tab. #11475
  • Data EditorLiterals in nested nodes ran off the edge of the page. #10854
  • Data Editorxsd:anyURI literals (URLs) were rendered inconsistently. #11353
  • SPARQLFederated queries against endpoints that return relative IRIs (such as the Linked Open Vocabularies endpoint) failed with a parse error instead of handling the relative IRI. #11445

entry.title: 26.4.300¶ (TriplyDB–Changelog)
entry.content:
Release date: 2026-04-30

Features

  • Console / API / TriplyDB.jsRenamed "organizations" to "groups" across the UI, API, TriplyDB.js, and CLI. Organizations were never required to map to a real-world organization — most instances use them to group users or resources for projects, environments (DTAP), or other purposes — and the new name reflects that. Features

  • Tabular uploadsIntroduced a new CSV/TSV import mechanism that preserves all information from the source files, enabling lossless roundtrip conversions between CSV and RDF representations. The new approach properly handles edge cases like duplicate column headers, multiple CSV files collapsing into the same graph, and hierarchical header structures. #10885

entry.title: 26.10.200¶ (TriplyDB–Technical changelog)
entry.content:
Release date: 2026-10-28

  • PreviewThe /oauth/register route is removed, from the API and the ingress: AI assistants identify themselves with a Client ID Metadata Document instead of registering. A migration deletes the authorization codes and refresh tokens of registered clients, so every connected assistant asks its user to authorize it once more. The API fetches a client's metadata document through the configured httpProxy.
  • Every line that the API, console, db, service and job pods write to their logs is one JSON entry, including stack traces, debug output and other console output, so a log collector no longer splits or merges entries. The db and service pods log one request entry per request, with its method, path, query, status and duration.
  • A new openTelemetry values block reports every error of the API, console, db, flow worker and job pods as an OpenTelemetry exception. Set openTelemetry.otlpEndpoint to an OTLP/HTTP endpoint to enable it, and openTelemetry.headersSecret to a Secret holding the exporter headers. The exporter does not use httpProxy: with network policies enabled, list the egress rules that reach the endpoint in openTelemetry.additionalEgress. Unset, nothing is reported.
  • Index jobs get a disk of at least indexJobs.minStorageGb (default 5) GB, whatever the size of the upload.
  • indexJobs.podSchedulingTimeoutSeconds no longer counts the time an index job spends pulling its image.
  • New values indexJobs.createHdtConcurrency and indexJobs.mergeHdtConcurrency (both default 1) set how many indices one upload, merge or update builds and combines at once. Each takes a CPU core and memory, so raise them only where both are to spare.
  • Saving a saved query runs it in the background to collect its statistics. That run is skipped when no Speedy worker is free, so it leaves workers to user queries. This avoids issues where many migrated queries affect the response time of other user queries. The new metric triplydb_api_speedy_skipped_background_runs_total counts the skipped runs.

entry.title: 26.10.100¶ (TriplyDB–Technical changelog)
entry.content:
Release date: 2026-10-14

  • BreakingThe values schema rejects several keys that this chart no longer has, so a helm upgrade with a values file that still sets one fails and names the key. Remove or move them before upgrading:
    • privacyMode: remove it. Anonymous visitors now see a user account only when that user owns a public dataset, saved query, story or SPARQL proxy, which covers most of what privacyMode: strict did. Only set adminSettings.maxAccessLevel to internal if the instance should hold no public content at all: it makes every public group and resource internal, which cannot be undone automatically.
    • orchestrator: remove it. The orchestrator Deployment, Service and NetworkPolicy are gone. Their successor, db, is disabled by default (db.enabled: false) and should stay disabled for now. This change will not impact your deployment.
  • BreakingGroups created without an explicit access level are private, where they used to be public. A script (TriplyDB.js, TriplyETL, the API) that creates a group and then a public dataset, query or story in it gets 403 Forbidden, because a resource cannot be more open than its group. Pass accessLevel: "public" when creating the group, or raise the default access level in the admin settings (or through adminSettings.defaultAccessLevel). Existing groups keep their access level.
  • Virtuoso services run Virtuoso 7.2.17 (previously 7.2.6)
  • BreakingWith networkPolicies.httpProxyEgressOnly enabled and an httpProxy configured, the virtuoso service pods lose their direct HTTP(S) egress as well. Virtuoso sends its outbound traffic through the proxy. This can be breaking, in situations where you have an older version of a virtuoso service running, and a 26.10.100 version (or higher) of the helm chart. In those cases, recreate the virtuoso services, to make sure they are upgraded as well.
  • A new adminSettings values block sets admin settings from the deployment configuration: passwordSignup, permittedSignupDomains, enforceTfa, oneActiveSessionOnly, maxAccessLevel, defaultAccessLevel. A setting given here is locked in the admin panel and refused through the API.
    • Lowering adminSettings.maxAccessLevel lowers every more open group and resource to it, which cannot be undone automatically.
  • New value sparql.blockSandboxProbes, default true. A client whose query tries to reach outside the SPARQL sandbox (sql: IRIs, bif: functions for file, HTTP or system access, a loopback SERVICE) is blocked for an hour from queries that can reach Virtuoso: queries on Virtuoso services and federated queries. They get 403 Forbidden. A logged-in client is identified by user, an anonymous one by IP address.
  • More outbound traffic honours the configured httpProxy: Google and GitHub sign-in, SERVICE clauses in SHACL rules, targets and conditions in flows, and index jobs fetching remote JSON-LD contexts. Index jobs get an index-job-http-proxy NetworkPolicy when a proxy is configured.
  • The API exposes Speedy worker pool metrics on its Prometheus metrics route: triplydb_api_speedy_workers, triplydb_api_speedy_tasks, triplydb_api_speedy_max_workers, triplydb_api_speedy_shed_tasks_total and triplydb_api_speedy_query_queue_wait_seconds. They replace the Analytics page in the admin settings and the /admin/speedyStats API route, which are removed. They are served in the Prometheus format, so Prometheus or any compatible monitoring tool can collect them. Set api.metrics.serviceMonitor.enabled to true (default false; this requires the Prometheus Operator CRDs) to have them scraped.

Patch releases

  • 26.10.105 · 2026-10-21
    • Breakingapi.metrics.serviceMonitor.networkPolicy and console.metrics.serviceMonitor.networkPolicy are replaced by a single list, networkPolicies.metricsIngressSelectors, of NetworkPolicy peers (podSelector, namespaceSelector, ipBlock) that may scrape the metrics ports of the API and the console. The values schema rejects the old keys. The list is empty by default, which admits no scraper, and it is independent of the serviceMonitor settings, so any collector can be admitted. With a ServiceMonitor enabled, add its scraper to the list, or scraping stops.

entry.title: 26.9.300¶ (TriplyDB–Technical changelog)
entry.content:
Release date: 2026-09-30

  • BreakingThe values schema rejects a number of api.env entries that the API no longer reads, so a helm upgrade with a values file that still sets one fails and names the key. Remove them before upgrading:
    • TRIPLY__DEFAULT_QUERY_PAGE_SIZE and TRIPLY__DEFAULT_CONSTRUCT_RETRIES: use the new values sparql.defaultPageSize (default 100) and sparql.constructRetries (default 10).
    • TRIPLY__EMAIL_ADDRESSES__NO_REPLY and TRIPLY__EMAIL_ADDRESSES__SUPPORT: use the new values email.addresses.noReply and email.addresses.support. TRIPLY__EMAIL_ADDRESSES__INFO has no replacement: the instance's contact email is used.
    • TRIPLY__MONGODB__CONNECTION_STRING and TRIPLY__MONGODB__PORT: use mongodb.secret.
    • TRIPLY__REDIS__HOST, TRIPLY__REDIS__PORT and TRIPLY__REDIS__CONNECTION_TYPE: use redis.*.
    • TRIPLY__JWT__SECRET, TRIPLY__JWT__EXPIRE, TRIPLY__JWT__RENEW_EVERY, TRIPLY__SOCKET_JWT__SECRET and TRIPLY__SOCKET_JWT__EXPIRE: session lifetimes come from sessions.timeoutsInSeconds, and the signing secrets are always the .jwt_secret and .socket_jwt_secret files on the storage volume, created on first start. An env-supplied secret was already written to that file, so existing sessions stay valid.
    • TRIPLY__TRIPLYDB_DEMO_LINK, TRIPLY__MAX_QUERY_RESULT_SIZE, TRIPLY__SHOW_MEMORY_USAGE_IN_DASHBOARD, TRIPLY__EMAIL_SILENT, TRIPLY__MIGRATIONS_STARTING_INDEX, and any name starting with TRIPLY__EMAIL_MESSAGE__ or TRIPLY__EMAIL_TEMPLATE_PARAMETERS__: remove them.

Set console.metrics.serviceMonitor.enabled to true to scrape it (this requires the Prometheus Operator CRDs). interval, scrapeTimeout and labels configure the ServiceMonitor, and console.metrics.serviceMonitor.networkPolicy.prometheusIngressSelector selects the Prometheus pods that the console's NetworkPolicy lets in. By default that is app.kubernetes.io/name: prometheus-agent in the monitoring namespace.

entry.title: 26.9.200¶ (TriplyDB–Technical changelog)
entry.content:
Release date: 2026-09-16

  • email.port is now defaulted where the api NetworkPolicy's SMTP egress rule is rendered: 465 when email.secure is true (the chart default), 587 otherwise. An unset email.port previously rendered a rule with an empty port and — with email.ip unset — no destination either, which allowed all TCP egress from the API pods to anywhere. If the SMTP server listens on another port, set email.port explicitly, or outgoing mail is blocked at the network layer.
  • api.pathTimeouts no longer defaults to an empty list. It now carries one entry, granting the graph-store endpoint (^/datasets/[^/]+/[^/]+/graph-store) an hour. A values file that sets api.pathTimeouts itself replaces the default wholesale, so repeat that entry there, or graph-store uploads fall back to api.timeout.
  • deploymentStrategy (on api, console, console.next and orchestrator) is validated against a schema, which accepts only type (RollingUpdate or Recreate) and rollingUpdate.maxSurge/rollingUpdate.maxUnavailable. Any other key is now rejected rather than passed through to the Deployment.
  • The graph store endpoint is a bulk-upload interface, so it is exempt from the general proxy timeout and from api.bodyLimitKb. On nginx that takes two additional Ingress objects, api-graph-store and console-api-proxy-graph-store, which match the path by regex and set request buffering off, no body-size limit, and an hour's timeout. On haproxy the same hour comes from a path_reg ACL in the api Service's backend-config snippet, which needs HAProxy 2.4 or newer for set-timeout client.
  • Optional chart values can be set to null to mean "unset", so a value that a shared values file supplies can be cleared without the key being removed.

entry.title: 26.8.200¶ (TriplyDB–Technical changelog)
entry.content:
Release date: 2026-08-20

  • BreakingThe private address ranges that the api and service NetworkPolicies exclude from outbound HTTP(S) have been widened: 172.16.0.0/20 became the full 172.16.0.0/12, and the link-local range 169.254.0.0/16 is now excluded as well. Requests from API, cron job and service pods to hosts in the newly excluded ranges — federated SPARQL endpoints, "download from URL" sources, webhook targets — are now blocked at the network layer. If such hosts are in use, allow them explicitly through networkPolicies.apiAdditionalEgress, or route them through an HTTP proxy (see below). Service pods have no additional-egress value of their own, so for those a proxy is the only route.
  • All ingresses whose latency ceiling is the API's — the api ingresses, and the console and console-beta root and /_api/ ingresses — now set an explicit proxy timeout, derived from api.timeout plus two seconds. They previously relied on the ingress controller's default, which is 60 seconds for nginx and 50 seconds for haproxy; on haproxy that silently undercut the default api.timeout of 58 seconds, so the controller severed the connection and returned its own 504 instead of the API's timeout response. If api.timeout is raised, the ingress timeouts now follow it automatically.
  • New value httpProxy.interface (default: ip). It selects how the proxy is addressed: ip uses httpProxy.ip as before, while service uses httpProxy.host (the hostname of a Kubernetes Service) together with httpProxy.namespaceLabels, the labels of the namespace the proxy runs in — a service address is translated to a pod address before a NetworkPolicy is evaluated, so the traffic must be permitted by namespace selector rather than by IP. The two sets of fields are mutually exclusive and the schema rejects mixing them. Existing values files that set httpProxy.ip need no change.
  • New value networkPolicies.httpProxyEgressOnly (default: false). When enabled, and a proxy is configured, the API pods' direct egress rule to external networks is dropped, so the proxy becomes the only route out. It has no effect when httpProxy is unconfigured.
  • More code paths now honour the configured httpProxy: dataset webhooks, avatar and image downloads, JSON-LD context resolution, file parsing in index jobs, and the Jena and Elasticsearch services. Virtuoso services are not covered (used in the context of federative queries), as that requires recreating them.

entry.content:
Release date: 2026-07-06

  • New value graphqlDescribeLruCacheSize (default: 1000). Independently bounds each of the GraphQL describe route's three in-memory LRU caches (outgoing predicates, incoming predicates, quad lookups). These caches speed up linked-data browsing; raise the value to cache more entries at the cost of memory per API pod.
  • The API ServiceMonitor now scrapes a second endpoint, /metrics/pod, on every API replica, in addition to the existing single-pod /metrics scrape. entry.title: 26.6.100¶ (TriplyDB–Technical changelog)
entry.content:
Release date: 2026-06-11

  • Two new values control the query-time vs. index-time trade-off for incremental uploads to existing graphs: indexJobs.mergeRatioThreshold (default: 10) and indexJobs.mergeAbsoluteThreshold (default: 10000). On an incremental upload, the existing index is folded into a new combined index only when it is at most mergeRatioThreshold times larger than the upload; indices smaller than mergeAbsoluteThreshold statements are always folded in regardless of the ratio. Raise mergeRatioThreshold to favour query speed, lower it to favour index-time on graphs that receive many small uploads. The defaults preserve the previous behaviour for most deployments.
  • The adminApiTokens flag now only governs static API tokens. OAuth access tokens are short-lived (1h) credentials minted through an interactive authorization grant and are treated like a web session, so they always carry admin privileges for admin users regardless of this flag. No action is required.

entry.title: 26.5.200¶ (TriplyDB–Technical changelog)
entry.content:
Release date: 2026-05-28

  • BreakingThe cert-manager HTTP-01 solver network policy is no longer hardcoded to the ingress-nginx namespace. The allow-cert-manager-resolver NetworkPolicy now derives its allowed ingress sources from the new networkPolicies.ingressSelector value and from any additionalIngress[].networkPolicySelector entries. If you deploy with network policies enabled and use cert-manager HTTP-01 ACME challenges behind an nginx ingress controller, you must now set networkPolicies.ingressSelector to a peer matching your ingress controller's namespace, e.g. { namespaceSelector: { matchLabels: { kubernetes.io/metadata.name: ingress-nginx } } }. Without it, the ACME HTTP-01 challenge can no longer reach the solver pod and certificate issuance/renewal will fail. The now-redundant acme.cert-manager.io/http01-ingress-class ingress annotation was removed as part of this rework.
  • New value api.pathTimeouts (default: []). Per-path timeout overrides: each entry maps a path prefix (must start with /) to a timeout in milliseconds. The longest matching prefix wins; when no prefix matches, the existing api.timeout applies.

entry.title: 26.5.100¶ (TriplyDB–Technical changelog)
entry.content:
Release date: 2026-05-14

  • New values block oauthServer with property maxRefreshTokenInactivityDays (default: 90). Configures the inactivity window for OAuth refresh tokens — each successful rotation resets the expiry to now + this many days. After this many days of inactivity the token expires and the user must re-consent.
  • The API ingress now exposes three new public OAuth 2.1 endpoints: /oauth/register, /oauth/token, and /oauth/revoke. These are used by OAuth clients. No action needed unless you have custom ingress overrides that restrict the routes exposed by the API.
  • Resolved a janitor regression that caused file cleanup to conflict with parallel TriplyDB operations and surface as transient errors in production.
  • Silenced an unactionable Redis subscriber error that was noisy in logs without indicating an actual failure.

entry.title: 26.4.300¶ (TriplyDB–Technical changelog)
entry.content:
Release date: 2026-04-30

  • BreakingThe addUser bin script flag -r, --role <role> has been replaced with -a, --admin <admin>, where the value is either site or super. Provisioning scripts that invoke addUser with --role must be updated to the new flag.
  • BreakingThe addOrg and deleteOrg bin scripts have been renamed to addGroup and deleteGroup as part of the organizations-to-groups rename. Update any operator scripts or runbooks that invoke these binaries.
  • HAProxy ingress on OpenShift: the haproxy.router.openshift.io/rewrite-target annotation for the /_api/web/auth/local/ route now uses /web/auth/local/ instead of /, fixing an authentication redirect bug on OpenShift HAProxy Router deployments. The default rewrite-target for other /_api/... routes remains /. No action is required for nginx or HAProxy community-controller deployments.

entry.title: 26.4.200¶ (TriplyDB–Technical changelog)
entry.content:
Release date: 2026-04-16

  • BreakingThe console.theme.material property has been removed from the values file. MUI theme colors are now derived from the existing console.theme properties directly (e.g., console.theme.primary, console.theme.secondary). If you have console.theme.material set in your values file, remove it — the deployment will fail validation otherwise.
  • New value flows.nodejsMemoryLimit (default: 5120, in MB). Controls the V8 --max-old-space-size for flow worker processes. Previously this was hardcoded. Increase this value if flow tasks process large datasets and run into out-of-memory errors.
  • Auth rate limiting ingress rules now target only /web/auth/local/ paths instead of the broader /web/ prefix. This prevents rate limiting of innocuous endpoints like logout, OAuth redirects, and session loading. No action needed unless you have custom ingress overrides referencing /web/ auth paths.
  • Added /web/, /__sm, and /sitemap.xml path routing to the console ingress for proper request routing.
  • HAProxy ingress improvements: updated rate limiting burst documentation and annotations for better accuracy.

entry.title: 26.4.100¶ (TriplyDB–Technical changelog)
entry.content:
Release date: 2026-04-01

  • Network policies for the API pod have been updated. A new rule allows API-to-API pod communication on the worker port, and additionalIngress entries with a networkPolicySelector are now included in ingress rules for both API and console pods. If you maintain custom network policies that override the chart defaults, review the updated templates.
  • The backup job now passes the MONGO_DB environment variable, sourced from the MongoDB secret (mongodb-database key) for external deployments or from mongodb.db for in-cluster deployments. This fixes backup failures when the database name differs from the default.
  • Removed the serverSelectionTimeoutMS MongoDB connection option. The default MongoDB driver timeout is now used, which improves behavior in environments with transient DNS or network delays.
  • Fixed JSON log timestamps to use the correct format.

entry.title: 26.3.200¶ (TriplyDB–Technical changelog)
entry.content:
Release date: 2026-03-19

  • Simplified the ingress path rewrite annotations for the /_api/ prefix. The generic ingress-annotation-rewrite helper has been replaced with a dedicated ingress-annotation-strip-api-prefix helper. This change is functionally equivalent for both nginx and HAProxy controllers, but if you have custom ingress overrides referencing the old helper name, they will need to be updated.
  • Added IDP certificate caching for SAML authentication. SAML identity provider certificates are now cached locally and refreshed periodically by a janitor task, reducing the number of outbound requests during authentication and improving resilience when the IDP metadata endpoint is temporarily unavailable.
  • Fixed the role attribute overwrite behavior for legacy SAML configurations.

entry.title: 26.3.100¶ (TriplyDB–Technical changelog)
entry.content:
Release date: 2026-03-04

  • New value api.bodyLimitKb has been added (default: 5120). This controls the maximum request body size in kilobytes for JSON, form, text, and SPARQL POST requests on external API routes.
  • Fixed an issue where the refresh-queries cronjob could hang indefinitely on certain saved queries, causing the entire cronjob to fail silently.
  • HAProxy rate limiting now correctly handles burst configuration by extending the rate-limit period, and both HAProxy and nginx now explicitly return HTTP 429 status codes for rate-limited requests.

entry.title: 26.2.200¶ (TriplyDB–Technical changelog)
entry.content:
Release date: 2026-02-18

  • BreakingThe ingress.proxyCacheName values is unused and has been removed. No migration needed, except for removing this property if it's set.
  • Next to Nginx, we now include full support for HAProxy ingress controllers as well. Ingress templates have been refactored to support both nginx and HAProxy ingress controllers. A new ingress.controller property (default: "nginx") controls which controller-specific annotations are generated. HAProxy support covers both the HAProxy Kubernetes Ingress Controller (haproxy.org/*) and OpenShift HAProxy Router (haproxy.router.openshift.io/*).
  • Fixed the console-api-proxy ingress rewrite rule for nginx. The path type is now ImplementationSpecific with regex pattern /_api/(.*) instead of a plain Prefix match, ensuring the rewrite-target correctly strips the /_api/ prefix.

entry.title: 25.10.300¶ (TriplyDB–Technical changelog)
entry.content:
Release date: 2025-10-29

  • SAML authentication attribute mapping configuration changed. The auth.saml[*].attributeMappings structure now supports additional properties for attribute updates. Added allowOverwrite boolean property to control whether attributes can be updated on subsequent logins (default: false). Added expiresAt and displayedName attribute mappings for temporary user accounts. Existing SAML configurations will continue to work as is
  • Added indexJobs.maxJsonLdFileSizeMb configuration property (default: 50). This limits the maximum size of JSON-LD files during index job processing to prevent memory issues with very large files. The environment API variable TRIPLY__JSONLD_MAX_BYTES_SIZE is not allowed anymore.

entry.title: 25.10.200¶ (TriplyDB–Technical changelog)
entry.content:
Release date: 2025-10-16

  • Node.js upgraded from version 22 to version 24. All TriplyDB container images now use Node.js 24 as the base runtime. This affects all pods including API, console, orchestrator, and job runners.
  • Redis upgraded from version 7.4.2 to 8.2.2 to address security vulnerabilities. Note that the security vulnerability in question could not have been abused in the context of the TriplyDB deployment.
  • Added indexJobs.legacyDelimitedFormat configuration property (default: true). This controls CSV/TSV import behavior. When set to true, uses the legacy simple format. When set to false, uses the new format which supports more complex table structures but produces more verbose RDF output.

entry.title: 25.3.100¶ (TriplyDB–Technical changelog)
entry.content:
Release date: 2025-03-06

Features

  • SAML can now be configured through native helm values, instead of using environment variables for the API pod. I.e., A configuration like this: 
    api:
  env:
    TRIPLY__SAML__0__ENTRY_POINT: some_entrypoint_url
    TRIPLY__SAML__0__IDP: some_idp_id
    TRIPLY__SAML__0__IDP_ATTRIBUTE_MAPPINGS__EMAIL__KEY: http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/emailaddress
    TRIPLY__SAML__0__IDP_ATTRIBUTE_MAPPINGS__NAME__KEY: http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/nameidentifier
    TRIPLY__SAML__0__ISSUER: some_issuer_id
    TRIPLY__SAML__0__LABEL: Login with SAML
    TRIPLY__SAML__0__SIGNATURE_ALGORITHM: RSA_SHA256
    TRIPLY__SAML__0__SUPPORT_IDP_LOGOUT: "false"
    TRIPLY__SAML__0__WANT_AUTHN_RESPONSE_SIGNED: "false"
    TRIPLY__SAML__0__IDP_CERT:
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef:
          name: saml-credentials-0
          key: CERT
    TRIPLY__SAML__0__PRIVATE_KEY:
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef:
          name: saml-credentials-0
          key: PRIVATE_KEY
    TRIPLY__SAML__0__PUBLIC_CERT:
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef:
          name: saml-credentials-0
          key: SIGNING_CERT
    TRIPLY__SAML__0__DECRYPTION_CERT:
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef:
          name: saml-credentials-0
          key: DECRYPTION_CERT
    TRIPLY__SAML__0__DECRYPTION_PVK:
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef:
          name: saml-credentials-0
          key: DECRYPTION_PVK
    will now be set like this: 
    auth:
  saml:
    some_idp_id:
      entryPoint: some_entrypoint_url
      issuer: some_issuer_id
      label: Login with SAML
      signatureAlgorithm: RSA_SHA256
      idpAttributeMappings:
        email:
          key: http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/emailaddress
        name:
          key: http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/nameidentifier
      additionalConfig:
        wantAuthnResponseSigned: false
        supportIdpLogout: false
      idpCertSecret:
        name: saml-credentials-0
        key: CERT
      spCertSecret:
        name: saml-sp-certs

Note that:

  • The IDP ID is now the key of the helm values object.
  • Certificates can only be set through secrets. For the IDP certificates this can be any secret with any field. For the SP certificate we expect a secret of type TLS, containing the private key and the public certificate.
